**Status: v0.1-draft. Not a stable standard.** This document specifies the
`.sframe` JSON Schema and its Derivative Citation Model. It is
language-agnostic: the schema and the algorithm below are implemented in R by
the surveyframe package, but nothing in this specification requires R, and the
reference validator (`validator/validate_sframe.py`) is written in Python
specifically to demonstrate that.

## 1. Scope

This specification defines two things:

1. The structure of a `.sframe` object: a typed survey research instrument
   (items, choice sets, scales, an analysis plan, and an optional measurement
   model) carrying a five-layer chained provenance manifest.
2. The Derivative Citation Model: how a `.sframe` object is rendered as a
   citation without ever being assigned its own DOI.

It does not define the surveyframe R package's internal implementation,
which is documented separately in that package.

### 1.1 Conformance profiles

Added 2026-08-22. The specification defines two profiles. An object is
conformant if it satisfies either.

| Profile | Schema file | Covers | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `instrument` | `schema/sframe-instrument.schema.json` | Layer 1 and the verification hash, serialised flat rather than nested under `layers` | implemented, surveyframe 0.4.0 |
| `full` | `schema/sframe.schema.json` | The complete five-layer chain of Section 2 | target; layers 3 to 5 arrive with surveyframe 0.6 |

The profiles exist because the two were previously out of step. The reference
validator passed this specification's own examples and rejected every real
file the reference implementation produced, failing on
`sframe_schema_version`, `layers` and `meta.author`. The five-layer model is
the target and is unchanged. The instrument profile records what is shipping,
so a consumer has something real to implement against today.

The reference validator selects the profile from the object's own shape and
reports which one it applied.

### 1.2 Format version

An object states its own format in `sframe_format`, a string of the form
`MAJOR.MINOR`, currently `1.0`. This is distinct from three other version
numbers in play, and the distinction matters:

| Field | Versions what |
|---|---|
| `sframe_format` | the file's structure |
| `sframe_schema_version` | the schema document (`full` profile only) |
| `version` / `meta.version` | the research instrument itself |
| the R package version | the implementation |

Consumers negotiate on `sframe_format`. Objects written before 2026-08-22
carry no such field and predate format versioning; they remain readable by
surveyframe but conform to neither profile.

## 2. The five-layer chain

| Layer | Name | What it covers | Hashed over |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Instrument | The instrument payload: items, choice sets, scales, branching, checks, analysis plan, model layer | content only (genesis-seeded) |
| 2 | Version / pre-registration | Lifecycle state and version transitions | content + Layer 1 hash |
| 3 | Response | Collected response data | content + Layer 2 hash |
| 4 | Analysis and reporting | Analysis results and the rendered report | content + Layer 3 hash |
| 5 | Verification manifest | The bundle of all four preceding layers | content + Layer 4 hash |

Each layer's hash is computed as:

```
layer_hash = SHA256(layer_content || previous_layer_hash)
```

Layer 1 has no preceding layer; it chains from a fixed genesis string instead
of a previous hash. This is a **chain**, not an independently-hashed set: the
Layer 5 hash is therefore sensitive to the order in which the prior four
layers occurred, not only to their content. An earlier design computed the
Layer 5 hash as `SHA256(sort(layer_hashes))`, which discarded ordering
information; this specification corrects that (see
`portfolio-planner/development_instructions/07_v08_v09_implementation.md` in
the wider surveyframe ecosystem for the implementation history, not required
reading to use this schema).

An object with fewer than five layers present is still schema-valid. It is
simply not fully citable (see `bibliographic.lifecycle_stage` below).

## 3. The Derivative Citation Model

A `.sframe` instrument is never assigned an independent DOI. Its identity is
the Layer 5 hash. Any citation generated from a `.sframe` object:

- carries the Layer 5 hash as its identifying string, not a DOI;
- carries exactly one DOI, if any — the parent software package's DOI, read
  from that package's own citation metadata at render time;
- is marked `[DRAFT]` / not fully citable if `lifecycle_stage` is less than
  `5/5`;
- carries a `parent_citation_lock`, a required field binding the instrument to
  its parent package's citation entry. An object without a complete
  `bibliographic` block, including this lock, fails schema validation.

This is deliberate: it keeps a stable, granular identifier (the hash) on
every research object without requiring a DOI-issuing authority to be
involved in every single instrument's lifecycle, while still keeping every
instrument traceable to one authoritative, DOI-bearing parent citation.

## 4. Mapping to existing standards

This schema does not replace DDI, CodeMeta, or PROV-O. It is narrower than
all three and maps onto them as follows.

| `.sframe` field | DDI (Data Documentation Initiative) | CodeMeta | PROV-O |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meta.title`, `meta.author` | `dc:title`, `dc:creator` | `codemeta:name`, `codemeta:author` | `prov:Entity` label |
| `layers.*.hash` | no direct equivalent (DDI has no chained-hash concept) | no direct equivalent | `prov:Entity` identity, chained via `prov:wasDerivedFrom` |
| `layers.*.timestamp` | `dc:date` | `codemeta:dateCreated` | `prov:generatedAtTime` |
| `layers.version` | DDI `VersionStatement` | `codemeta:version` | `prov:wasRevisionOf` |
| `layers.response` | DDI `PhysicalInstance` / data file description | no direct equivalent | `prov:Entity` generated by a `prov:Activity` (collection) |
| `bibliographic.parent_citation_lock` | no direct equivalent | `codemeta:isPartOf` | `prov:wasDerivedFrom` (instrument -> package) |

This mapping is provisional for v0.1-draft and will be checked against the
DDI Codebook/DDI-Lifecycle and CodeMeta crosswalk tools before 1.0.

## 5. Validation rules

0. `sframe_format`, where present, must match `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`. Its
   absence indicates an object written before format versioning.
1. `sframe_schema_version` must match the schema version in use
   (`full` profile only; the `instrument` profile uses `sframe_format`).
2. `meta.author[].orcid`, if present, must match the ORCID checksum pattern.
3. Each present entry under `layers` must have `hash` matching `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`.
4. Layer chaining: for any two adjacent present layers (in the fixed order
   instrument -> version -> response -> analysis_reporting ->
   verification_manifest), the later layer's `previous_hash` must equal the
   earlier layer's `hash`. Non-adjacent gaps (e.g. instrument and
   analysis_reporting present, version absent) are schema-valid but flagged by
   the reference validator as an incomplete chain, not a broken one.
5. `bibliographic`, if present, must include `parent_citation_lock`. An
   instrument may exist and validate without a `bibliographic` block at all
   (e.g. mid-collection); it simply cannot be cited yet.

## 6. Status and next steps

v0.2-draft, 2026-08-22. The `instrument` profile is validated against real
output from surveyframe 0.4.0, replacing the synthetic examples the previous
draft relied on. The `full` profile remains unvalidated against a real
five-layer object, because layers 3 to 5 are not implemented; those arrive
with surveyframe 0.6 (renumbered 2026-08-19 from the former 0.9).

Before 1.0:

- Validate the `full` profile against real surveyframe 0.6 output, not
  synthetic examples.
- Complete the DDI/CodeMeta/PROV-O crosswalk check in Section 4.
- Register a FAIRsharing "Standard" record.
- Freeze `sframe_schema_version` at `1.0`.
